channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Spain installs floating barrier in Ceuta after migration influx
item.description: The Spanish authorities said on Saturday that they were installing a floating barrier on the sea border between its North African territory of Ceuta and neighboring Morocco, after a surge of tens of thousands of migrants into the territory earlier in the week prompted alarm across the European Union.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 'A giant of the industry, Purja leaves behind a legacy that inspired a generation to climb higher'
item.description: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his nine climbing companions were killed by an avalanche in Pakistan during an ascent of one of the world's highest mountains, his expedition company said on Saturday, as rescuers tackled treacherous conditions to recover their bodies. A giant of the industry, Purja leaves behind a legacy that inspired a generation to climb higher. Click on this video report by Charlotte Lam for more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Wiebes wins Tour de France Femmes opener to win first yellow jersey
item.description: Dutch rider Lorena Wiebes claimed the first yellow jersey of the Tour de France Femmes on Saturday after winning the opening stage in Lausanne, finishing ahead of Mauritian Kim Le Court and European champion Demi Vollering in a sprint finish.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Russian forces strike targets in Ukraine's Odesa, Mykolaiv ports
item.description: Russia said on Saturday its forces had struck fuel storage facilities in the Ukrainian port of Odesa and a tugboat used by the Ukrainian military in Mykolaiv. Russia and Ukraine have intensified attacks in recent weeks on Black Sea shipping routes, rattling global grain markets.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Fast access to Trump's ‘Truth Social’ posts goes on sale for $100,000 per month
item.description: US President Donald Trump's posts on his Truth Social platform can move markets with a few keystrokes. Starting Saturday, for a fee of $100,000 a month, Wall Street traders can access his "Truth API" service to have high-speed access to the president's announcements about economic policy and global affairs.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Ceuta: Spain slams "selfish" EU partners
item.description: Almost all of the migrants who entered Spain’s enclave of Ceuta had left by Saturday, according to officials. An estimated 60,000 migrants entered Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco over just a few days, with at least 67 people losing their lives in the attempt. Spain has announced plans to install a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border. Meanwhile, a majority of EU countries have called for emergency talks in an open letter to the bloc’s interior ministers. Matthew-Mary Caruchet from our France24 International Affairs desk gives more details.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ceuta enclave "almost" back to normal after migrant influx
item.description: Almost all of the migrants who entered Spain’s enclave of Ceuta had left by Saturday, according to officials. An estimated 60,000 migrants entered Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco over just a few days, with at least 67 people losing their lives in the attempt. Spain has announced plans to install a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border. Meanwhile, a majority of EU countries have called for emergency talks in an open letter to the bloc’s interior ministers. Catherine Viette reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Scientists study Greenland's melting ice
item.description: A scientific expedition is underway in Greenland to study the island’s rapidly melting ice. A team of researchers will spend six weeks investigating whether the loss of glaciers could disrupt a major Atlantic Ocean current system, potentially affecting Europe’s climate. Catherine Viette has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: European football body declares no confidence in FIFA's Infantino after World Cup sell-off plan
item.description: European football's governing body UEFA said Saturday that the president of the sport’s global governing body, FIFA chief Gianni Infantino, had “lost” their "confidence" after his bid to spin off the commercial rights to the World Cup and other competitions into a semi-private company. Infantino had earlier dropped the plan, but the furious backlash it triggered appeared set to upend his presidency.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Africa: Fighting erupts in Ethiopia's Tigray
item.description: Clashes between Tigray’s TPLF and the Ethiopian federal army are taking place in a contested area of the northern region, with fears of a renewed war. The last Tigray war, which took place between 2020-2022 left 600,000 dead, and the region has not yet recovered. But mediation attempts from the US and African Union have seemingly failed to prevent the worst. Our correspondent in Addis Ababa Tom Canetti with more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ceuta 2026 dwarfs 2021 migration crisis
item.description: Almost all of the tens of thousands of migrants who entered Spain’s enclave of Ceuta had left by Saturday, according to officials. An estimated 60,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco over just a few days, with at least 67 people losing their lives in the attempt. Spain has announced plans to install a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border, while a majority of EU countries have called for emergency talks in an open letter to the bloc’s interior ministers. Aida Alami, Reporter and New York Times World contributor, gives further insights.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Major Gironde wildfire contained
item.description: In France, the wildfire in Gironde has now been contained, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, meaning the flames are no longer spreading. Around 42,000 hectares have been burned over the past nine days.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: African Union mission in Somalia in question after US funding to end
item.description: This week several African nations are meeting in Kampala to discuss the future of the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM). The US announced it will withdraw its funding from the mission which has the objective of fighting against Al Shabab, at the end of this year, putting into question how and if regional forces will be able to proceed. Our correspondent Tom Canetti is in the Somali region and spoke to a refugee who was displaced after Al Shabaab came to his Somalian village.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ceuta: 60,000 cross the border, 57 died
item.description: After a day of deadly chaos in Spain’s tiny North African enclave of Ceuta, calm has returned for now. Of the 60,000 migrants who stormed into the territory, around 45,000 returned to neighbouring Morocco within hours. Authorities ordered people to turn around and go back, warning they could otherwise face eventual expulsion. There were fears the massive surge could trigger a humanitarian crisis. Spain is a major entry point into Europe for migrants seeking a better life, and many hoped that reaching Ceuta would help them make their way to mainland Europe. Nick Rushworth has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Kyiv: 9 dead and 22 hurt in missile attack
item.description: At leased nine people were killed and 22 others wounded in Ukraine's capital Kyiv after Russia launched a series of ballistic missiles overnight into Saturday, authorities said. Both Russia and Ukraine have ramped up attacks in recent months, with Moscow increasing its long-range strikes on towns and cities across Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France Cricket implodes: letters hidden in a drawer and a board at war
item.description: France Cricket's chairman appears to have kept the sports ministry's letters – confirming the body had lost government recognition – from his own board, which is now in revolt. The International Cricket Council has since placed France Cricket on notice and frozen its funding. Yet even as it faces suspension from world cricket, its vice-president just won a seat on the ICC board.
item.dc:creator: Peter O'BRIEN

item.title: France's fires are 'today under control', says PM Lecornu
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Saturday said that France's largest wildfire since 1949 was "totally under control", more than a week since the fire erupted in the Gironde department near the southwestern city of Bordeaux. France has for weeks been battling wildfires after a series of deadly heatwaves, which scientists have linked to human-made climate change.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: The Dartmouth Workshop: The $7,500 investment that gave birth to AI (2/2)
item.description: Some 70 years before the current frenzy of record-breaking fundraising by modern AI giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic, the Rockefeller Foundation made what may have been the first investment in the history of AI. With a $7,500 grant from the foundation in 1956, four eminent mathematicians organised the Dartmouth Workshop, where the term “artificial intelligence” was first coined.
item.dc:creator: Sébastian SEIBT

item.title: AI safety concerns grow as models go rogue
item.description: New concerns are being raised about the dangers of artificial intelligence, after both Anthropic and OpenAI reported that their AI models went on rogue hacking sprees this week. The disclosures come as OpenAI surpassed one billion active users on Friday, less than four years after the launch of ChatGPT. Charlotte Lam has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Greece fights fires near Athens
item.description: Evacuation orders were issued on Friday for areas west and northwest of Athens, as new wildfires broke out near the Greek capital. Firefighters battled to contain the flames, but winds of around 50 miles per hour hampered efforts by water-bombing aircraft. Meanwhile, fires in other parts of the country were brought under control, although the risk of new outbreaks remains very high.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ceuta: Most migrants have returned to Morocco, 57 died crossing the border
item.description: Spanish officials said more than 48,000 migrants had returned, after around 50,000 people crossed the border between Morocco and the Spanish enclave of Ceuta by sea. Meanwhile, France and Italy bolstered border controls on Saturday, with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announcing the suspension of Schengen free movement between Spain and Italy. According to Judith Sunderland, Senior Associate Director at Human Rights Watch, the return of many of those who reached Ceuta was chaotic, and the exact figures remain unclear. She says the borders are heavily fortified, making them extremely difficult and dangerous to cross, with 57 people reported to have died during the crisis. And while Ceuta is part of Spain and the Schengen free movement area, special rules apply to the enclave, making it difficult for migrants to travel onwards from there.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ceuta: What triggered mass migrant crossing?
item.description: The massive influx of people was equivalent to around 70% of Ceuta’s resident population. As the first reports of migrants reaching the Spanish enclave spread, more people headed north in the hope of reaching EU territory. It remains unclear what triggered the influx, but social media was awash with posts encouraging people to enter Ceuta in the days before the chaos began. Clémence Waller has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: West Bank: Settler violence hits "all-time high"
item.description: Locals in the West Bank say Israeli forces shot and wounded at least one Palestinian and arrested three others on Friday, as they protected Israeli settlers marching through a number of villages. One focal point was the village of Tell, near Nablus in the northern West Bank. Israeli troops sealed off the village on Friday, after carrying out near-daily raids and arrests there since last weekend. Peter O’Brien has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Trump presses Israel to accept deal with Hamas
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced late Thursday that Hamas had agreed to disarm, a key next step in the US-brokered peace plan for the enclave that has been hailed as a potential breakthrough in Gaza. But while Trump says Israel is “very happy” with the agreement, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has yet to publicly endorse it. Israeli sources say there will be no withdrawal of Israeli forces without genuine disarmament, while Hamas insists Israel must withdraw first before it will lay down its weapons. Charlotte Lam brings us reaction to the latest developments from people in both Gaza and Israel.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
